title: feat(ui): the shell runs in a browser - eframe web runner, awaited GPU start-up (#31 rung 3)
body:
Rung 3 of #31 (M13.3), **retargeted to `main`; was stacked on #841** (it still contains #841's commits until that PR merges): the CamCraft shell now **runs in a browser**. This is a partial step (`Refs #31`): there is no file picker and no in-browser CI job yet.

## Review round (head `b6483d66`)

Fixes for the review of `1f903bd4`, as one plain commit on the same branch:

1. **Diagnostics reach the browser console.** New `crates/ui/src/diag.rs`: `diag_warn!` / `diag_info!` print to stderr / stdout natively, exactly as before, and call `console.warn` / `console.log` on wasm32, where std drops both streams. The stock eye's fall-back to the CPU march (`trace/eye.rs`), the file dialog's "cancelled" note and the other direct prints in browser-compiled UI code now go through it: 35 sites in 12 files. A law test fails on any direct print outside the seam, the native-only files and the tests. No new dependency: the console binding is eframe's re-exported web-sys.
2. **`poll_oneoff` does what its comment says.** It now succeeds at once, reports each clock subscription as elapsed (the caller's sleep is over) and writes the first skipped wait to the console with its length. A descriptor subscription gets an ENOTSUP event, also said in the console. It used to answer ENOSYS.
3. **The missing-imports message prints.** The import list is read with `|| true`, so an empty list reaches the named `die` instead of ending the script through pipefail.
4. **The wasm-bindgen install is announced and can be refused.** See the maintainer section below.
5. **The shim answers the nine imports and nothing else.** `fd_read`, the environ calls and the other unused exports are removed; the build already fails by name if the module asks for a tenth. Unknown clock ids answer EINVAL and a write, close or seek on a descriptor that is not open answers EBADF, each with one console warning. The two expected probe answers (ESPIPE for a seek on stdout, EBADF ending the preopen walk) are documented and not reported.
6. **The first browser target is clamped.** `view_pass::target_extent` now holds the pixel ratio to 0.1..=8 itself (1 for NaN), so no caller can size a zero or runaway target. The existing `target_extent_is_never_zero...` test covers zero, negative, huge, infinite and NaN ratios.

Re-proved after the fixes: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on head `b6483d66` fell back to batch: **all 9 steps ok, 0 failed (55.3 min)**, including the ui suites and `clippy -D warnings` on all eight crates. The gate ran on the branch as pushed; it still merges cleanly with `origin/main`, so no merge of main was taken.

`web/build-app-wasm.sh` exited 0 again (it installed the pinned CLI after printing what it would run). Headless Chrome, same rules as before, drew the first frame and opened the Stock page on a click. The stock-eye refusal now arrives as a console **warning**: `stock eye: the device binds no storage buffers to a fragment shader - the deviate sheet stands in`.

Not shown in the browser: the exact `eye.rs` line the review named ("the CPU march stands in"). On WebGL2 the composite refuses first, so the whole eye is refused and that line is never reached; it goes through the same macro as the line that did appear. `poll_oneoff` was not called during start-up either; the shim was checked in Node against a fake memory instead (16 checks, including the event layout and each console warning). The `CAMCRAFT_WASM_NO_INSTALL=1` refusal was not run.

Left open: camcraft-app's own diagnostics (its `tracing` events and direct prints) are still dropped in a browser - they need a console writer installed by the browser shell. Added to the owed list.

## What changed

- **Browser runner: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell_web.rs` (new, wasm32 only).** An `eframe::App` over a `<canvas>` whose frame runs the same `shell::shell_layout` as the native window. The page starts it through one export, `camcraft_start(canvas_id)`. eframe's web runner was chosen over our own canvas glue because it was already in `Cargo.lock`, its web half needs no egui-winit, and it already does the DOM events, canvas sizing and awaited GPU start-up (about 4000 lines we would otherwise write and maintain). The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/31-wasm-web-runner.md`.
- **Shared 3D pass: `egui_app/view_pass.rs` (new).** The scene upload gate, target sizing, the View3D + traced-stock pass and the repaint law moved out of the native frame, unchanged, so the two shells cannot drift. `shell_window.rs` and `shell_window/frame.rs` now call it (frame.rs 409 -> 358 lines).
- **GPU waits that await.** `TracePass::new`, `Composite::new`, `StockEye::new` and `headless_gpu::device` each got an `*_async` twin holding the unchanged body with `.await` at the wait. The blocking forms are thin `pollster::block_on` wrappers, `cfg(not(wasm32))`, so native behaviour is unchanged. `pollster` is now a native-only dependency: a blocking wait in shared code no longer compiles for wasm32. The browser shell builds the stock eye on the event loop after its first frame and picks it up from a slot.
- **`trace/readback.rs` (new, native only).** `TracePass::trace` and `decode` moved there unchanged; `trace.rs` goes from 411 to 343 lines.
- **Native-only entries refuse by name on wasm32.** The `--headless` proof joins the windowed entry behind the same refusal; `shell::headless` is `cfg(not(wasm32))`.
- **Never a panic at start-up.** A missing canvas, a refused adapter or surface, or a runner without a device ends as text in `#camcraft-status` (`data-state="refused"`) plus a console error. The page turns uncaught errors and rejections into the same message.

## Dependency / script / workflow changes (needs-maintainer)

- `Cargo.toml` [workspace.dependencies]: `eframe = "=0.36.2"` (no default features; `wgpu`, `default_fonts`), `wasm-bindgen = "0.2.129"`, `wasm-bindgen-futures = "0.4"`. **No new crate enters the tree**: all three were already in `Cargo.lock` (eframe through egui_kittest, the others through wgpu). The lock diff is three lines, camcraft-ui's dependency list. All MIT OR Apache-2.0.
- `crates/ui/Cargo.toml`: those three as **wasm32-only** dependencies; `pollster` moved to the native-only table.
- `web/build-app-wasm.sh`: step 4 now links the UI as a cdylib (`cargo rustc -p camcraft-ui --lib --crate-type cdylib`, manifest unchanged) because an export does not survive the link of the binary. New step 5 runs the wasm-bindgen CLI whose version it reads from `Cargo.lock` (a matching one on PATH, else `cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version <lock version> --locked` from crates.io into `target/wasm-tools/bindgen`, never `~/.cargo`). **For the maintainer to decide:** that install downloads and builds the CLI and its dependencies, its build scripts run, and the CLI has no checksum in this repo. The script prints the exact command before running it, and `CAMCRAFT_WASM_NO_INSTALL=1` turns it into a refusal that names the version to put on PATH, copies the page and shim into `target/web/`, and fails if the module asks for a WASI import the shim does not export. **The `camcraft-ui` binary is no longer linked for wasm32** (#841 linked it); the cdylib replaces it.
- `web/index.html` (new): the page - canvas, status element, import map, module script.
- `web/wasi_shim.js` (new): answers exactly the nine `wasi_snapshot_preview1` imports the wasi libc under flecs asks for (clocks from the page, stdout/stderr to the console, a skipped wait for `poll_oneoff`, a named errno for the rest; `proc_exit` throws). Refusals and skipped waits are written to the console once each.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: **comment only** on the existing `wasm` job. Triggers unchanged (`workflow_dispatch` only). That job will now also install the wasm-bindgen CLI when it is run.

## How it was proved

- **In a browser (this machine, 2026-11-11).** `web/build-app-wasm.sh` exited 0 on the final tree and printed:
  - `linked .../debug/camcraft-cli.wasm`
  - `linked .../debug/camcraft_ui.wasm` (647 MB debug; 62 MB after wasm-bindgen)
  - `WASI imports answered by the shim: clock_time_get fd_close fd_fdstat_get fd_prestat_dir_name fd_prestat_get fd_seek fd_write poll_oneoff proc_exit`
  - `page ready in .../target/web`

  Chrome was then run headless only (`--headless=new --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`, throwaway profile, a loopback static server on 127.0.0.1, driven over the DevTools protocol). Console and DOM read back:
  - `gpu: adapter "ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device ...)" via gl`
  - `camcraft-web: runner started`
  - `stock eye: the device binds no storage buffers to a fragment shader - the deviate sheet stands in`
  - `camcraft-web: first frame drawn (viewport target 600x400)`
  - status element: `data-state="running"`, document title `CamCraft - Untitled`, canvas 1264x705.

  A screenshot showed the whole shell: ribbon with icons, browser tree, viewport with the origin axes and view cube, properties pane, status line. A synthetic click on the ribbon's Stock door then opened the Stock page and selected Stock in the tree, so input, the command queue and the flecs world all work in the tab. The screenshot is kept out of the repo.

  One line was added to `web/index.html` after that run (an empty `rel="icon"` link, to stop the favicon 404); the page was not re-run for it.
- **Native gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/31-wasm-ui-shell` on head `1f903bd4` fell back to batch (Cargo change): **all 9 steps ok, 0 failed (35.3 min)** - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui (cwd crates/ui) suites, and `clippy -D warnings` on all eight crates.
- **Pinning tests (native):** `diag::tests::shared_ui_code_prints_only_through_the_diag_seam`, `diag::tests::the_macros_take_println_shaped_arguments`, `view_pass::tests::target_extent_is_never_zero_and_scales_with_the_pixel_ratio`, `view_pass::tests::a_browser_frame_with_no_egui_timer_still_follows_the_document`. The moved `shell_window::redraw_tests` still run against the moved `redraw_delay`. The existing GPU suites run the blocking wrappers over the new async bodies.

## Not exercised

- **WebGPU.** Headless Chrome offered no WebGPU adapter here, with or without the software-adapter flags, so wgpu ran on WebGL2. The awaited stock eye was refused by name *before* its await, so an error scope actually awaited in a browser has not been seen. The `*_async` bodies are exercised natively through their blocking wrappers only.
- **Refusal paths in the browser** (no adapter at all, missing canvas, `proc_exit`): written, not triggered.
- **Anything past the first frame and one click**: importing a model, generating a toolpath, simulation, posting, keyboard and text input, resizing. Opening and saving cannot work yet (`file_dialog` answers "cancelled" on wasm32).
- **Thread sites.** No code changed: every spawn already goes through `thread::Builder::spawn` and handles the error (import runs inline; playback and the CPU eye refuse by name), and generation goes through rayon. None of this was run in the browser.
- **A release build** of the page, and the `wasm` CI job itself.
- The native GUI was not launched (by rule).

## Still owed on #31

1. An async file picker behind `file_dialog`, so a model can be opened and a program saved.
2. An inline playback path where the worker cannot spawn (today it refuses by name), and a browser check of generate/import.
3. The in-browser CI job (manual trigger), and the Pages deployment (#688).
4. A WebGPU run, to see the awaited stock eye land.
5. `lib.rs` still allows dead code on wasm32: 17 native-only helpers (gpu_select, the backend mask, `world::seed`, the recent-files read) have no caller there and need gating one by one.
6. A console writer for camcraft-app's `tracing` events and direct prints, which a browser still drops.
7. `shell.rs` is still 923 lines (only an import and a `cfg` changed here); the viewport panel is the seam to split.

Changelog: CamCraft's shell runs in a browser: eframe web runner over a canvas, awaited GPU start-up, page and WASI shim built by web/build-app-wasm.sh (file picker and CI job still owed) (#31, PR #847)

Effort: max (dispatched above the issue's `effort:high` label; no escalation)

Refs #31
